deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The previous page solves x^7 - 3x^2 + C = 0 for C = 2 - 5*sqrt(2)(1+i) and C = -2 - 5*sqrt(2)(1+i). These C lie on lines Re C - Im C = +/-2, i.e. lines parallel to 1+i, which is presumably what 'Parallele' means. By recomputing roots, I identify the two equations on this page as members of the family C = 2 - t(1+i):
- 'Gleichung 4 der dritten Parallele': C = 2 - sqrt(2) - sqrt(2) i. Then |C| = 4 sin 22.5 deg = 1.530734, log|C| = 0.1848997, arg C = -67.5 deg.
- 'Gleichung 3': C = 2 - 2i. Then |C| = 2*sqrt(2), log|C| = 0.4515450, arg C = -45 deg.
- For comparison, equation 5 on the next page has |C| = 3.6955 (log 0.5676753), which corresponds to t = 2 + sqrt(2).
The page heading says 'the remaining roots': one root of equation 4, at 145 deg 59'38.091'', was improved at the end of p. 231, and others came from earlier sheets.

METHOD (my modern restatement). Put x = rho e^{i phi}, with rho real and allowed to be negative (Gauss's 'n'), and C = |C| e^{i gamma}.
- Multiply the equation by e^{-2i phi} and take the imaginary part: rho^7 sin 5phi = |C| sin(2phi - gamma).
- Multiply by e^{-7i phi} and take the imaginary part: 3 rho^2 sin 5phi = |C| sin(7phi - gamma).
- Eliminating rho via (rho^2)^7 = (rho^7)^2 gives a single equation for phi:
  F(phi) := 7 log|sin(7phi - gamma)| - 2 log|sin(2phi - gamma)| - 5 log|sin 5phi| = 7 log 3 - 5 log|C| =: T.
- With gamma = -67.5 deg the arguments are 2phi + 67.5, 5phi and 7phi + 67.5. Example for phi = 37 deg 39'59'': 142 deg 49'58'', 188 deg 19'55'', 331 deg 9'53''.
- With gamma = -45 deg (equation 3) the shift is +45 deg.
- Targets: T = 3.3398488 - 0.9244985 = 2.4153503 for equation 4, and T = 3.3398488 - 2.2577250 = 1.0821238 for equation 3. The latter is the number written at the head of the right column.

COLUMN LAYOUT. Each column takes a trial angle phi to the nearest second and lists:
- log sin of the three arguments, each with its tabular difference per 1'' of that argument (in units of the 7th decimal);
- 2 log sin(2phi - gamma), 5 log sin 5phi, their sum, and 7 log sin(7phi - gamma). The attached derivatives are multiplied by 4, 25 and 49 (chain rule times power);
- F(phi) together with dF/dphi per second.
The secant correction is delta = (T - F)/F'. The column then forms log rho^7 = log sin(2phi - gamma) - log sin 5phi + log|C|, corrected by delta times its derivative, and divides by 7 to get log rho. Finally log rho + log cos phi and log rho + log sin phi give Re x and Im x.

RESULTS, equation 4:
- phi = 37 deg 39'59.163''. F = 2.4154377, F' = -5355.6, delta = +0.163''. log rho^7 = 0.6200354 n, log rho = 0.1149907 n. x = -1.0315732 - 0.7963071 i.
- phi = 70 deg 41'39.894''. F = 2.4154243, F' = +6956.4, delta = -0.106''. log rho = 0.1161764. x = 0.4320039 + 1.2332241 i.
- phi = 104 deg 17'2.198''. F = 2.4153145, F' = 1804.5, delta = +0.198''. log rho = 0.0970241 n. x = 0.3084904 - 1.2116743 i.

CHECK TABLE for equation 4. It lists all 7 roots (angle, log|rho|, Re, Im) and verifies Vieta's relations.
- Sum of roots = 0, since there is no x^6 term. The pairs are summed as (x1+x2) = 0.2038449 - 0.7126298 i, (x3+x4) = 0.7404943 + 0.0215498 i, (x5+x6+x7) = -0.9443389 + 0.6910797 i. The total residual is about +3 and -3 units of the 7th decimal.
- Product of roots = -C. The log moduli add to 0.1848994 against log|C| = 0.1848997, a difference of -3. The angles add to 292 deg 29'59.986'' against 292 deg 30' (= -67.5 deg), a difference of -0.014''. Taking the three negative-rho roots into account, the product's argument is 112.5 deg = arg(-C).

RIGHT COLUMN, equation 3 (C = 2 - 2i), same procedure:
- phi = 39 deg 44'21.567''. F = 1.0819996, delta = -0.433''. log rho = 0.1231063 n. x = -1.0209602 - 0.8488053 i.
- phi = 71 deg 27'42.102''. F = 1.0819017, F' = 21857.4, delta = 0.102''. log rho = 0.1313189. x = 0.4301919 + 1.2828571 i. The first value 1.2830148 i was struck and corrected.
- phi = 103 deg 13'4.425''. F = 1.0820346, F' = 2099.9, delta = 0.425''. log rho = 0.1172208 n. x = 0.2995032 - 1.2751466 i.
These roots are collected and checked by Vieta on p. 233.

PURPOSE. The page is a numerical tabulation of all roots of x^7 - 3x^2 + C as C runs along parallel lines. Presumably this traces root paths, plausibly connected with Gauss's 1816 work on the fundamental theorem (the bundle name) or with the trinomial-equation method he later published in 1849/50. That purpose is my inference.
errors: Eq. 4, second column: 7 x 9.5802893 = 67.0620251, but the page has 7.0620351, an excess of 100 units in the 7th decimal. I recomputed log sin 22 deg 21'40'' = 9.5802893, so the log-sine itself is right. With the correct value F = 2.4154143 and delta = -0.092'' instead of -0.106'', so the root angle 70 deg 41'39.894'' should be about 70 deg 41'39.908''. This accounts exactly for the -0.014'' deficit in Gauss's own angle-sum check (292 deg 29'59.986'' vs 292 deg 30').
Eq. 3, first column: 25 x 62.2 = 1555, not the 1550 written, so the sum derivative is -1497 and F' = -2873.9. The effect on delta is about 0.0007'' and is negligible.

Eq. 3, third root: the derivative of log rho^7 should be 2(7.1) + 5(47.5) = 251.7 per second. Gauss apparently used 2(7.1) + 2(47.5) = 109.2 (the marginal '109.2'), giving a correction of +46 instead of about +107. log rho is therefore too small by about 9 units of the 8th place. This plausibly explains the '-9' residual in the log-modulus product check on p. 233. The inference is tentative.
Eq. 3, second root: the imaginary part was first given as 1.2830148 i, which is wrong. log rho + log sin phi = 0.1081783 gives 1.2828571, which Gauss himself substituted.

Otherwise every log multiple, sum, difference, derivative combination and secant correction checks: 874/5355.6 = 0.163, 740/6956.4 = 0.106, 358/1804.5 = 0.198, 2221/21857.4 = 0.102, and 0.8049351/7 = 0.1149907, among others.

results.what: Trigonometric/logarithmic solution of a trinomial equation x^7 - 3x^2 + C = 0 with complex C. Write x = rho e^{i phi}, reduce to the single transcendental equation 7 log sin(7phi - gamma) - 2 log sin(2phi - gamma) - 5 log sin 5phi = 7 log 3 - 5 log|C|, solve by tabular differences, then recover rho from rho^7 = |C| sin(2phi - gamma)/sin 5phi.
results.modern_name: Polar-coordinate (amplitude/argument) numerical root finding for trinomial equations; secant/regula-falsi iteration with log tables
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss, Beiträge zur Theorie der algebraischen Gleichungen (1849/50), on trinomial equations

results.what: Verification of the computed roots by Vieta's relations: sum of roots = 0 and product = -C, checked in modulus via summed logs and in argument via summed angles.
Systematic tabulation of all 7 roots of x^7 - 3x^2 + C for C moving along lines parallel to 1+i (C = 2 - t(1+i)), presumably to follow root trajectories.
results.modern_name: Root locus / continuation of roots under a parameter (numerical homotopy-style tabulation)
results.usually_credited_to: Root-locus ideas are formalised much later (Evans 1948 in control theory); continuity of roots under parameter change is classical (Cauchy, Weierstrass)

deep.surprise_reason: The method is Gauss's own published trinomial technique with ordinary log-table computation and Vieta checks. The only mildly interesting features are the systematic numerical tracking of roots of a degree-7 polynomial with complex constant along parallel lines (an early 'root locus' tabulation) and the internal consistency of the slips with his own checks. Nothing here is a new theorem.
